assign.notes: I read the split file only, not the FixFlow or testbed sources. Where an idea touched both repositories I followed the repository its working code lives in. Three calls were close. check#16 (MAC-29) went to WP1 because a production-dump restore is recovery work rather than a gate. tokens#19 (TOK-19) went to WP5 because its problem is tokens burned by waiting lanes. check#44 (MEM-41) went to WP7 because it belongs to the knowledge-store design. check#10~s1 (CHK-36) could also sit in WP4, since its ticks are a ship-plan convention. assign.notes: All 78 ideas assigned: 45 WP3 (gate/merge/fix-round/board/audit scripts and FixFlow PR review), 26 WP10a (skeptic, refuter, critique and register method in research/design workflows), 6 WP6b (knowledge-store diff lookup, gate-runner, withholding), 1 outside (method#38 shape block to WP4). check.notes:
I checked all 78 assignments against the records in docs/program/evidence/harness-compile/data/gate/split-WP3.md and found none clearly wrong under the WP3, WP10a and WP6b definitions.

One reason text is wrong, though the package is right. method#16 is "Root as the only writer of shared documents", which is WP3's single-writer rule. Its stated reason ("Code counts and scores; finding-table principle") describes review#44 instead.

Some assignments are borderline but not clearly wrong. Each is FixFlow phase-routine work and might sit better in a phase-routine package like WP4, where method#38 went:
- review#43: clean worktree check at phase close
- check#33: stop after three identical CI failures
- measure#57: audit of the phase routine's seven obligations
- review#42: orchestrator verifies owner-stated facts inline during phases, not inside research workflows

check#47, the caller-pin pytest, needs no store and lands in FixFlow CI. It was still designed in the knowledge store's D17 to cover the store's blind spot, so WP6b holds.

method#14, parallel#8 and review#60 are FixFlow ship-plan rules that the coordinator owns. WP3's definition names them anyway: the single-writer rule, merge holds and drain branches.

assign.notes: All 67 ideas assigned. Two moved out: skills#25 to WP1 and method#54 (map store) to WP7. Four were close calls. method#37 (save-rule plus skill retirement) went to WP10a because its problem is unsaved workflows. skills#14 (invoke orchestration skill) went to WP10b as a skill-trigger check. method#57 (observer, spend control, HumanLayer skills) is a mixed idea, placed in WP10a. skills#21 (BAML) went to WP10a as schema tooling. check.notes: I agree with all 67 assignments. Two things to check.
